title: Quarter Plan: Velocity Map for Hosted API - Model Catalog Connections
creator: Lena Cho
description:
Objective: produce an executable quarter plan that aligns Hosted API capacity, model lineup cadence, and evaluation gates. The deliverable is a velocity map that ties OKRs to concrete sprint-level milestones: model onboarding windows, canary adoption targets, and capacity hedges for peak cohort demand.

Scope: align product, infra, and research on (1) prioritized model candidates for hosted exposure, (2) canary schedule with rollback windows, (3) autoscale buffer thresholds for Dedicated and Hosted, and (4) eval plans for quality regressions tied to prompt suites. This ticket covers planning artifacts, stakeholder sign-off, and a handoff bundle for engineering execution.

Metrics / OKRs: target a 20% reduction in mean 95th latency for high-throughput endpoints (OKR-Host-1), maintain model-level quality regression rate <1% across the catalog (OKR-Model-2), and keep capacity commit variance within ±10% of forecast (OKR-Infra-3). Each milestone in the velocity map will map to an owner and a success criterion.

Decisions & trade-offs: we will favor a staggered canary that sequences models by risk (latency-sensitive first) instead of a single-wave rollout to limit blast radius. Trade-offs include slightly longer overall rollout time vs. lower incident risk. For high-cost models, recommend a hybrid rollback policy that falls back to a quantized variant to preserve availability.

Artifacts and links: planning deck (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Velocity+Map+Q2), tentative sprint calendar (Google Sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/hostedapi-q2-plan), eval harness PR (GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/218), preliminary capacity sim (internal Grafana board link).

Acceptance criteria: 1) velocity map with per-sprint commitments and owners published to Confluence; 2) cross-functional sign-off from Eng, Research, Console, and SRE; 3) a prioritized list of model candidates with gating criteria; 4) a contingency playbook for capacity shortfalls.

Risks: model regressions after swap, unexpected demand surges for new endpoints, gating tests that are flaky. Mitigations: dedicate an early canary window, expand smoke evals, pre-provision short-term burst capacity for high-risk cohorts.
